summary: Across both the 2014 and 2023 mayoral campaigns, Olivia Chow has consistently positioned transit as a core priority, calling for stable long-term investment, improved bus service, and accessible TTC stations (CtiJjtEA_dw, 67bmXJOtGB, tQqAqWOtEK, tGazGDutPq). In 2014, Chow backed light rail projects including the Scarborough LRT, Finch West LRT, and Sheppard East LRT, opposed the Ford-Tory subway alternative, and supported GO electrification and fare integration (t2bRE6OtJ0, tnpNLvutDi, uo9OStutNY, tI4_ksutP4, ogAfBlutOi). In 2023, Chow called for reversing TTC service cuts, keeping fares affordable, and announced a dedicated Scarborough busway from Kennedy Station to Scarborough Town Centre funded by savings from converting the eastern Gardiner to a boulevard (CswVZjUAkFp, CryXD1ULOhA). Chow has also pledged bike lane expansion and committed to starting work on a subway relief line (pemGDZOtPs, uZbnNbutFW).

key_positions.stance: Supports stable, long-term investment in public transit and treats transit infrastructure as urgent
Supports improved bus service as an immediate priority
Supports reversing TTC service cuts and keeping transit affordable, safe, and reliable
Supported light rail projects (Scarborough LRT, Finch West LRT, Sheppard East LRT) in 2014 and opposed the Ford-Tory subway alternative
Supports GO electrification and regional fare integration
Supports a dedicated Scarborough busway from Kennedy Station to Scarborough Town Centre, funded by savings from converting the eastern Gardiner to a ground-level boulevard
Supports building the subway relief line
Supports adding more new subway cars to the TTC fleet

key_actions.action: Unveiled a transit map at campaign headquarters in August 2014
Announced a Better Bus Service plan in 2014 and repeatedly pressed for improved bus service at Jane-Wilson
Made a 2014 announcement on improving traffic flow
Announced a Scarborough busway plan in May 2023 promising 20 minutes daily commute savings, using the existing RT corridor and new bus-only lanes
